messages:
lina: Kicking off calypso9b-int4 onboarding. Ran full summarization bench overnight — baseline fp16 vs int4 shows similar perplexity but summaries are ~10% shorter on average.
jun: short summaries = red flag. any obvious tokenization mismatch?
lina: quick diff shows more frequent EOS tokens inserted early. tokenizer vocab looks OK but calypso has a trailing-sentinel token (id 50255) that our converter might be remapping.
alex: also saw rotary mismatch when loading with our runtime: headwise rotations look scaled down. could be theta/scale expectations.
maria: can you dump rotary params + tokenizer headmap?
lina: dumped both. snippet:
```
# model meta
"rotary_freq": 10000,
"rotary_scale": 0.9993,
"vocab_size": 50256,
"eos_token_id": 50255
```
and our importer currently normalizes rotary_theta -> 1000 for older models.
jun: aha. that theta normalization would compress phases -> different phase at long positions => earlier EOS via decoder confidence shifts.
alex: can we try importing keeping rotary_freq untouched and re-run quantized kernel?
lina: started a quick job with importer flag `--preserve-rotary` and int4 calibration pinned. running command:
```
./scripts/onboard.sh --model calypso9b-int4 --quant int4 --preserve-rotary --batch 4
```
ci-bot: build 2026.03.21-172999 took the job: https://ci.internal/runs/172999-24 (logs uploaded) :eyes:
maria: while that runs, I checked the tokenizer mapping: conversion script folded case and merged some diacritics. calypso's tokenizer expects NFKC-disabled for pretokenization. so our normalizer is probably collapsing sequences that should remain distinct.
jun: so two possible levers: keep original tokenizer normalization + preserve rotary params. both might fix length bias.
lina: repro numbers from last night (fp16 vs int4 default-import):
- ROUGE-L fp16: 0.372
- ROUGE-L int4 (default): 0.338
- avg summary length fp16: 132 tokens
- avg summary length int4: 119 tokens
- EOS frequency per 1k tokens: fp16 2.1 -> int4 3.4
alex: big delta. if preserve-rotary + keep tokenizer normalization off brings rouge back near fp16 then quant pipeline is fine; else it's a quantization bias.
lina: job finished with --preserve-rotary: initial numbers look promising — ROUGE-L 0.365, avg length 129. still slightly off but much closer.
maria: next step: re-run with original tokenizer (disable NFKC and casefold) and do int4 calibration sweep (per-channel scales).
jun: assign follow-ups: @lina rerun tokenizer-off sweep and attach eval artifacts; @alex trim the quant kernels if needed; @maria prepare a short PR to keep `--preserve-rotary` default for calypso family until we have automation to detect theta ranges.
lina: will run sweep now. ETA ~2h. linking issue: <https://tracker/redwood/ML-789>
alex: if sweep shows residual regressions, we should run a small hallucination-oriented eval (QA) to ensure factuality not impacted by token splits.
maria: agree. also add a note to docs about tokenizer pretokenization flags for calypso family.
jun: thanks team. small wins so far. :party_parrot:
